text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Finnish papers this morning.
HELSINGIN SANOMAT
- To many Finnish voters in the coming local elections, an ideal local government representative is well educated, supports job creation and defends womens' rights.
- Police want more controls on importers of Harley Davidson motorbikes, suspected of irregularities.
- Parliament unanimously passed law granting small loans to service sector business.
- Over 50 candidates for coming EU elections are campaigning on the Internet with little costs -- but do they have a large enough audience?

- Government to seek clarification on joining the arms production wing of the WEU, WEAG. Under-Secretary Jaakko Blomberg told parliament foreign affairs committee that membership would not affect Finland's foreign policy line.
- AMMULEHTI
- Conductor Sakari Oramo to replace Sir Simon Rattle as leader of famous Birmingham Symphony orchestra in 1998.
- Demand for influenza vaccines unexpectedly exceeded estimates.
- TURUN SANOMAT
- A major reason for students interrupting studies is to get access to unemployment benefits.
KAUPPALEHTI
- The government and state-owned Sisu disagree on the price tag on Sisu's defence materials unit which the government is to merge into its new defence materials group.
- UPM-Kymmene and Enso silent on profit outlook this year, after Metsa-Serla warned it would make a loss in May-December.
- Tamro would lose market share if Finnish pharmacies lost their monopoly position.
- Second-quarter growth in private consumption was slower than expected, Statistics Finland official says.
- Finnish banks have narrowed the efficiency gap against Swedish rivals and come out of the banking crisis, senior Bank of Finland official says.
DEMARI
- Less generous terms of employment would not bring new jobs, says Labour Minister Liisa Jaakonsaari.
- Cheapest flight from Helsinki to Brussels goes via Prague.
-- Helsinki newsroom +35 80 6805 0247
